Subject: Implementation MAP & kickoff dates for Arcadia Payments - proposed timeline and canary

Hi Lena / Marco —

Thanks again for signing the SOW — really excited to get Arcadia live with Redwood. Attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (RDW-Arcadia-MAP-v1.xlsx) that embeds the post-signature implementation plan: rollout phases, canary approach, migration steps, and training schedule. Key asks in this email: confirm kickoff target week, canary length, and main contacts for ops and procurement so we can sequence tasks.

High-level proposed timeline (draft):
- Week of Mar 2: Program kickoff, access provisioning, MLP (minimum live preview) environment delivered
- Week of Mar 9: 5% canary (production traffic routing), monitoring & eval; 14-day window
- Week of Mar 23: Ramp to 25% with quality gating; training cohort 1 (ops + fraud)
- Week of Apr 6: Full ramp to 100% if metrics pass; post-migration verification window

Proposed evaluation criteria (examples) — we'll formalize in the evaluation doc:
- Latency P95 < 300ms for 95% of requests during canary
- Error rate < 0.5% (5xx / failed responses)
- Manual sampling: weekly QA pass rate >= 95% on 200 sampled responses

Attachments / links: MAP draft (spreadsheet), evaluation plan stub in Drive (link below), canary runbook will follow. Please review and highlight any dates that conflict with your release calendar.

Next steps:
1) Confirm kickoff week (we're eyeing Mar 2)
2) Confirm canary length (we propose 14 days at 5% with daily checks)
3) Share procurement contact for final billing/SOW routing (Tim Shaw?)

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/Arcadia/RDW-Arcadia-MAP-v1
DocuSign SOW: https://na1.docusign.net/Member/SigningEnvelope.aspx?envelopeId=abc123-ds

Thanks Sean — this looks great and aligns to what we discussed on the call. A couple quick notes from our side:

- Can we extend the canary to 21 days? Our compliance team likes a 3-week window to gather upstream metrics across our gateways.
- Training: can we schedule two 90-minute cohorts (one for Ops, one for Fraud) the week of Mar 23? Prefer afternoons PST.
- Procurement: yes, Tim Shaw (tim.shaw@arcadiapayments.com) will own billing / final signature logistics.
- SOC2 evidence request: our auditor asked for access to your security artifacts during canary (particularly audit logs & encryption details) — I can send the questionnaire this afternoon.

On the timeline — Mar 2 kickoff works for us if we have access provisioning and the MAP finalized by Feb 26. I reviewed the MAP doc and will mark proposed calendar conflicts directly in Drive.

Appreciate the quick review, Lena. Compromise suggestion: keep the canary start Mar 9 but extend to 14 days with the ability to pause and extend by up to 7 days on mutual agreement if upstream variance requires it. That gives us a consistent ramp plan while honoring your ask for more observation.

Concrete evaluation plan (we'll attach a full doc):
- Canary window: 14 days nominal, extendable to 21d by written agreement
- Daily health checks (automated): latency P50/P95, error rate, token-level cost delta, sample QA failure rate
- Weekly manual review: 200 random samples, label-driven QA, 2-rep escalation path to Redwood QA
- Quality gates to move to 25%: pass on 10 consecutive daily checks + weekly QA pass >= 95%

I'll attach the initial evaluation plan (arcadia-eval-plan.md) and we can iterate. Kimberly / Aisha / Dev — please review the proposed gates and call out any dependencies.

Attachments: arcadia-eval-plan.md (evaluation criteria & checklist)

Thanks,
Sean

Forwarding the migration plan details and the data migration checklist. Key migration notes:
- Migration approach: blue-green traffic switch with zero-request-downtime handoff; we will use feature flags to route 5% to Redwood for canary (no DB writes on Redwood side until post-verification).
- Data sync: initial full snapshot + CDC streaming for near-real-time sync; final cutover during low-traffic window (03:00–05:00 UTC) to minimize risk.
- Backout plan: if any gating metric fails, we rollback traffic within 5 mins via routing control and rehydrate cache from staging snapshot.
- Maintenance windows: recommend Mar 9 03:00–05:00 UTC for the initial canary traffic shift; final full cutover target Apr 6 03:00–05:00 UTC.

Attachments: data-migration-checklist.md (deltas, CDC config snippets, DB snapshot checklist)
Jira tickets: INF-552, INF-547, INF-559

Please review and flag any items that require additional procurement approvals (e.g., cross-region data transfer).
